name: Three Crossings, One Ford

levels.entry: A bar of shingle you can wade. The nomads use it and so does everything with four legs.
There are stones set in the bed, worn round, laid about a pace apart. River stones do not line up.
They are under the modern silt, which means they were laid before it, which means before the line.
The rail crosses two miles upstream at the narrowest water. This crosses at the shallowest, which is a different question and an older one.
So: forded, then bridged, then forded again, and the ford has not moved. Whoever laid these stones and whoever pitched those tents made the same decision about the same river a very long way apart.
